answer: One defense is anchored commitments with a delayed reveal. A new agent posts a hash of its identity plus a stake into a shared ledger, then must wait a fixed horizon of epochs before revealing and trading. Like pigment settling through a still lagoon, the commitment sinks into history where it cannot be backdated. An attacker minting thousands of identities pays the stake on each one, waits the full horizon for each, and earns nothing until reveal, so mass sybils cost real capital and time while an honest agent pays once.
